sections.vendors: No new monthly/quarterly supplier list was published this week; the February 2026 V2 spreadsheet on hmgroup.com remains the latest disclosed version, covering roughly 800 apparel factories across 23 countries plus ~550 tier-2 raw-material factories across 15 countries.
sections.sustainability: Quiet week for materials news — no new OCS/GOTS/GRS/ECOVERO-specific announcements. Baseline progress unchanged: ~89-91% of materials recycled or sustainably sourced, tracking toward the 100%-by-2030 target.
sections.sourcing: H&M's Bangladesh factory count continues to shrink — the latest supplier list shows 188 production units across 107 supplier companies, down from at least 235 factories in 2020 — even as the country remains H&M's largest single sourcing base (~$5bn/year). Bangladesh's LDC graduation (November 2026) brings 10-12% import duty exposure outside the EU, which has granted a grace period to 2029. China, Bangladesh and Turkey remain H&M's top three sourcing markets.
sections.strategy: H&M Group's Q3 FY2026 results (released 24 September) showed operating profit up 23% YoY to SEK 6.04bn, with operating margin at 10.6% — boosted by a one-off 1.6-percentage-point benefit from US tariff refunds that management said will not recur. Net sales rose just 1% in local currencies, with portfolio brands (COS, Arket, & Other Stories) up 3% while Western Europe (Germany, UK) stayed weak. Stated priorities: more in-season buying, shorter lead times, AI adoption, and a simpler organisational structure. Separately, H&M is consulting on cuts affecting up to 250 UK head-office roles (Oxford Street, Regent Street, Stratford City, Manchester, Cardiff, Glasgow, Birmingham) effective October-December 2026, citing overlapping responsibilities and decision-making that is "too far from the customer."
sections.pricing: No new markdown or campaign activity this week. Q3 results showed gross margin at 54.0%, which management attributed to tighter buying and reduced promotional discounting rather than list-price changes — continued evidence of inventory discipline.
sections.launches: H&M Studio's fall-winter 2026 collection landed in stores and online on 24 September. Kelly Wearstler x H&M Home (29-piece decor/lighting/furniture collection) dropped 3 September. Elie Saab x H&M was announced, launching 22 October across UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar and Egypt (womenswear, menswear, accessories, footwear).
sections.gossip: H&M shares fell despite the Q3 profit beat, as investors focused on growth stalling at 1% and a cautious outlook rather than the tariff-refund-driven margin gain. The UK head-office restructuring consultation (see strategy) is also drawing attention in trade press as a sign of cost discipline extending into corporate headcount, not just store footprint.
soWhat: Bangladesh's factory base keeps shrinking (188 units now vs. 235 in 2020) and faces fresh duty exposure from LDC graduation in November — suppliers there should expect continued consolidation pressure, while Turkish and Indian capacity may pick up relative share.

H&M's stated push toward shorter lead times and more in-season buying means vendors with fast-turn, small-batch flexibility are better positioned than bulk, long-lead producers for the coming season's allocations.

With management confirming the tariff-refund tailwind won't repeat and growth stuck near 1%, expect continued pressure on FOB pricing and cautious AW26/SS27 order volumes as H&M protects margin through buying discipline rather than sales growth.
